canDo: Can express different degrees of certainty and conjecture accurately when discussing science and climate (il est certain que / il est probable que / il se peut que / il semble que / devoir for conjecture / the conditional for caution), and tell how sure an author is of their information in articles and broadcasts.
review: Review day 3’s “indicative or subjunctive” (il est probable que + indicative / il est possible que + subjunctive) and day 10’s past conditional (for unconfirmed information); combine with day 18’s pronouns: il se peut qu’on en sauve une partie.
input: Read: an analysis of attribution science, a column defending “scientific doubt” and a botanist answering readers’ questions — label every statement with its degree of certainty (certain / very likely / possible / uncertain); listen: a glaciologist on Alpine glaciers, a “true or false” segment distinguishing weather from climate and a heat warning news flash — note the words speakers use to show how sure they are.
output: Write: a ≥220-word article for a magazine’s “science explained” column, explaining that “scientific uncertainty is not ignorance”, with at least 5 different expressions of modality; speak: a 4-minute monologue on “geoengineering”, then defend “climate lessons in primary school” in the debate.
checkpoint: Reading and listening accuracy ≥80%; can tell il semble que + subjunctive from il me semble que + indicative, and sans doute (probably) from sans aucun doute (without any doubt); article ≥220 words with accurate modality; a 4-minute monologue without breaking off.
challenge: Today’s challenge: find a news item on RFI’s « Journal en français facile » or TV5MONDE about climate or scientific research, and write 3 sentences giving information that is “certain”, “very likely” and “still uncertain” (e.g. « Il est certain que… / Il se peut que… »), or record a 1-minute spoken commentary.

questions.why: The article presents in turn the principle of attribution science, its conclusions (certain / fairly certain / uncertain) and its uses. It says explicitly that some conclusions « restent fragiles », so B goes too far; the author doesn’t criticise the models (C).
« pour les tempêtes ou les tornades, les conclusions restent fragiles »; the conclusion on heatwaves is « sans appel », and the link with heavy rainfall « solide ».
« cette nuance passe mal dans le débat public »: some think scientists know nothing, others blame every thunderstorm on the climate — two extremes.
« en partie » means “partly”: more and more events will have a contribution from global warming, but it won’t be the only cause. A contradicts “oui”, B contradicts “en partie”.
« ce langage prudent n’est pas un défaut de la science, mais sa principale qualité », and the ending argues for teaching everyone to “read uncertainty”.
« C’est précisément ce qui la rend digne de confiance : elle peut être corrigée »; C is the opposite of “provisional conclusions”.
« Il appartient plutôt aux médias, et à l’école, d’apprendre à chacun à lire une incertitude »; to C he answers « Sans doute pas ».
The layout is « Question de Martine » + « Réponse de Yannick Perrot, botaniste » — an expert answering a reader.
« Il est très probable que la hausse des températures moyennes en est la principale cause ». In C, « uniquement » goes too far.
The interview covers in turn the observations, the causes, forecasts and the effects on people in the valleys. Tourism is only one of the consequences.
« une perte d’épaisseur de près de quatre mètres en une seule saison »; one metre was the figure for a “bad year” twenty years ago (A is a distractor).
« il a peu neigé en hiver, et il semble que des poussières venues du Sahara aient noirci la neige » (il semble que + past subjunctive).
« la plupart devraient disparaître d’ici à la fin du siècle, quoi que l’on fasse »; “cutting emissions may save some of them” refers to the large glaciers (B is a distractor).
The segment is called « Vrai ou faux ? » and checks a sentence circulating on social media.
« Le climat, c’est une moyenne sur au moins trente ans »; A says the opposite.
« presque une année sur deux » + « ces gelées font davantage de dégâts » because plants start growing earlier.
« l’auteur de la phrase devait être de bonne foi »: devoir for conjecture = he was probably sincere.
« pourrait durer jusqu’à dimanche ; il se peut même qu’il se prolonge […] mais cela reste à confirmer »: both the conditional and il se peut que express uncertainty.
« l’arrosage des jardins est interdit entre huit heures et vingt heures »; sport is only “advised against” in the hottest hours, not banned outright.

V19-01.exZh: Researchers always state the degree of confidence in their conclusions.

V19-02.exZh: The results of this new study are conclusive.

V19-03.exZh: It is unlikely there will still be ice on this summit by 2100.

V19-04.exZh: Acknowledging the limits of your research isn’t admitting weakness.

V19-05.exZh: Overly technical information doesn’t get across to the general public.

V19-06.exZh: Every accident brings the question of cycle lane safety back up.

V19-07.exZh: The minister used a lot of careful wording before announcing the measure.

V19-08.zh: as things stand, in the current state of knowledge
V19-08.exZh: As things stand, the risk seems limited.

V19-09.exZh: For a long time, some manufacturers tried to keep doubt alive about the dangers of their products.

V19-10.exZh: It is up to the public authorities to protect the most vulnerable.

V19-11.exZh: For years, the merchants of doubt delayed the ban on this pesticide.

V19-12.zh: to be careful not to, to avoid
V19-12.exZh: Be careful not to draw conclusions from a single case.

V19-13.exZh: A late frost destroyed part of the region’s vineyards.

V19-14.exZh: Through citizen science, thousands of people count the birds in their gardens.

V19-15.exZh: The images of the collapsing glacier made a strong impression.

V19-16.exZh: Despite a cold winter, the underlying trend is still warming.

V19-17.exZh: Whatever we do, some small glaciers will disappear.

V19-18.exZh: For coral reefs, every tenth of a degree counts.

V19-19.exZh: If the forecasters are to be believed, this summer will be very dry.

V19-20.exZh: He was mistaken, but probably in good faith.

V19-21.zh: to be put on orange alert
V19-21.exZh: Three départements were put on orange alert overnight.

V19-22.exZh: The episode may go on longer, but that remains to be confirmed.

V19-23.exZh: For lack of a simple solution, researchers are exploring a new avenue.

V19-24.exZh: To make room for this new subject, the curriculum had to be trimmed.

V19-25.exZh: He states categorically things that have never been checked.

title: Certainty and conjecture
